thread:
ravi: heads up — brought HIVE-embeds (oak+stork ensemble) into staging with int8 quant. quick smoke shows a recall@10 drop on the curated holdout. asking for eyeballs :eyes: https://redwood-internal/embeds/hive/staging

olivia: which holdout did you use? the curated-search-2025 one?

ravi: yep — curated-search-2025 (5k queries). baseline float32 ensemble was oak+stork combined with simple avg weighting. int8 run used per-tensor quant then ensemble avg.

dom: can you paste the numbers? even a tiny table helps.

ravi: quick paste from eval run:
```
model                   recall@1   recall@10   ndcg@10   silhouette
hive-ensemble-fp32      0.682      0.913       0.821     0.042
hive-ensemble-int8      0.665      0.851       0.790     -0.003
```

priya: that silhouette drop is worrying — UMAP shows oak/stork points mixing more than before. clustering quality degraded for small clusters (k<=8).

henry: did you use per-channel quantization for both models? per-tensor on one model + per-channel on the other will cause scale mismatch in ensemble averages.

ravi: int8 run used per-tensor both to keep runtime simple. i can repro with per-channel — good call.

ml-ci-bot: CI: embed-eval-holdout/4912345678 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/hive-int8/4912345678/results.json

dom: try weighting scheme instead of raw avg: normalize each vector by its L2 before combining or compute weighted sum with learned alpha. simple formula we used earlier:
```
combined = normalize(w1 * v_oak + w2 * v_stork)
w = softmax([alpha_oak, alpha_stork])
```

priya: also try ensemble at score level: compute cosine(query, v_model) per model then weighted sum of scores. that avoids vector scale mismatches.

henry: if you want to keep vector-ensemble, rescale using the float32 mean norm per model (store calibration stats). e.g., scale_int8 = scale_fp32 * (mean_norm_fp32 / mean_norm_int8).

ravi: OK i'll run three variants: per-channel quant both, score-level weighting, and calibrated rescale + avg. ETA ~2hrs.

zara: for canary, prefer score-level weighting — safest from a regression perspective. roll back to fp32 if any customer impact.

ravi: noted. running now. will post results (and small eval command for reproducibility):
```
./eval_embeddings.py --models oak,stork --ensemble hive-avg --quant int8 --calibrate --holdout curated-search-2025.csv --k 10 --metrics recall,ndcg,silhouette --out s3://redwood-ci/hive-int8/4912345678/
```

ml-ci-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/hive-int8/4912345678/summary.csv

priya: if the recall@10 gap stays >4% absolute, let's open a quick RFC before pushing to dedicated. we should capture example queries where stork dominates vs oak.

ravi: will dump the top-50 failure queries and share. thanks all :pray:
